NONE: › to cover an area of ground with a hard, flat surface of pieces of stone, concrete, or bricks
鋪，築（地面）

example: The area near the beach is paved with bricks set in patterns.
靠近海灘的這片區域是用拼花磚鋪就的。

NONE: C2 If something paves the way for/to something else, it makes the other thing possible.
（為…）鋪平道路，（為…）創造條件

example: Scientists hope that data from the probe will pave the way for a more detailed exploration of Mars.
科學家希望探測船傳回的數據會為更深入的火星探索提供條件。

NONE: › used about a city to mean that it is easy to make money there
（某個城市）遍地是黃金，極容易發財

example: Unemployed youngsters still come to London thinking that the streets are paved with gold.
失業的年輕人繼續成百上千地來到倫敦，認為這裡遍地都是黃金。

NONE: B1 UK US sidewalk a path with a hard surface on one or both sides of a road, that people walk on
人行道
B2 US the surface of a road when it has been covered with concrete or tarmac
鋪築過的路面

example: Keep to the pavement, Rosie, there's a good girl.
沿著人行道走，羅茜，乖孩子。

NONE: › a person who draws pictures on a pavement using coloured chalks, especially so that people who walk past will give small amounts of money
（用彩色粉筆在人行道上作畫討錢的）街頭畫家
› a flat piece of stone, usually used in groups to cover a path or an area
鋪路石

C: › UK a building near a sports field, especially one where cricket is played, used by the players and sometimes by people watching the game
（尤指板球場旁設立的）選手席，看臺
› US one of a group of related buildings
（一組相關建築物的）分館，配樓
› US a large building in which sports or entertainments take place
› a temporary structure, such as a large tent, especially used at public events or for shows
（尤指用於公共活動或展覽的）臨時建築物（如大帳篷）

example: the West Pavilion of Central General Hospital

NONE: › a paved area, or material used to pave an area
鋪過的地面；鋪築材料
› a flat piece of stone, usually used in groups to cover a path or an area
鋪路石
› a sweet cold dish consisting of a meringue (= the transparent part of an egg cooked slowly with sugar) with a layer of fruit and cream on top
鮮奶油蛋白甜餅
